newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, shrug off jump in JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends flat, shrug off jump in JGBs.

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen futures ended flat on Tuesday compared with their Friday close.
Euroyen futures are heavy at the top, and received little effect from the steep jump in Japanese government bond futures, a brokerage trader said.
The settlement figures for Tuesday's day session were not immediately available due to system failure, an official at the Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange said.
A TIFFE official said the start of the night session and the tallying of the open interest figures were also expected to take place later than usual.
TIFFE's night session is usually from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m. (0700 GMT to 0900 GMT).
Monday was a national holiday and markets were closed.
The result of the U.S. presidential election is unlikely to have any effect on the Euroyen futures market, the brokerage trader said.
Only if U.S. stocks and bonds move after the election, will there be any effect on Japanese financial markets, he said.
"If U.S. Treasuries fall sharply, this could lead to a fall in JGBs, which may depress Euroyen futures," the trader said.
The key overnight call rate stood at 0.47 percent as of 0724 GMT, up from Friday's weighted average of 0.46 percent.
A city bank trader said the overnight call rate had eased on Friday, ahead of the weekend, and that it rose back up again at the start of a new week.
There was less upward pressure on days such as Tuesday, which used to be designated as bond settlement days, ever since rolling settlement for JGBs started in October, the trader said.
JGB settlement formerly took place on fixed dates -- the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and 30th of each month.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
Trading hours for Euroyen futures on TIFFE were extended from Tuesday to a total of 7-1/2 hours from seven hours.
The new trading hours are 9 a.m. to 11.30 a.m. (0000 GMT to 0230 GMT) in the morning and 12.30 p.m. to 3.30 p.m. (0330 GMT to 0630 GMT) in the afternoon.
About 70 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit were issued on Tuesday, a regional bank trader said.
